subject: Vendor lineage & data transfer matrix request
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@pangearetail.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@pangearetail.com, security@pangearetail.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor lineage & data transfer matrix request

Hi Sofia,

We are running a short vendor review ahead of our procurement kickoff for the Redwood Labs integration. As part of our risk assessment we need the following by EOD Friday: a vendor lineage spreadsheet (who does what), a CSV data-transfer matrix (which subprocessors handle customer data and whether they access PII), and copies or links to your most recent SOC 2 Type II report and dataflow diagram.

Specific questions to cover in the CSV:
- Subprocessor name and purpose
- Does the subprocessor access customer content or PII? (yes/no)
- Data residency (does data leave the US?)
- Encryption in transit & at rest (Y/N + short note)
- Any subprocessors that perform model training or fine-tuning on customer-provided inputs

We have a template attached (pangea_vendor_lineage_template.csv) — please populate if possible. If parts of this require an NDA or an on-demand redaction, flag them in your response.

Thanks — this will help our security team triage the onboarding path.

Regards,
Maria Lopez
Security Engineer, Pangea Retail
Maria.Lopez@pangearetail.com

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@pangearetail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor lineage & data transfer matrix request

Hi Maria,

Thanks for the clear template — attaching a completed CSV and a short evidence pack to get you started. Attached: redwood_subprocessors_inventory_2026-07.csv (filled per your columns), redwood-dataflow-diagram-2026-07.png, and a link to our most recent SOC 2 Type II report (redwood-soc2-type2-2025.pdf).

Quick answers to your bullets to help triage:
- Subprocessors: we’ve listed all third parties that process customer requests on our behalf (compute providers, telemetry vendors, monitoring, and managed inference partners).
- Access to PII/customer content: each row indicates whether a subprocessor may access customer content. For Hosted API customers some metrics/telemetry are processed by monitoring partners; no hosted subprocessors perform customer-initiated model training.
- Data residency: Hosted API customers can select region routing; subprocessors that provide global CDN or telemetry may process metadata outside the US. Dedicated and Private deployments keep data in customer-controlled environments per contract.
- Encryption: All data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest we use AES-256 for persistent storage. For Hosted we manage keys; Dedicated/Private can use customer KMS/HSM.

Two notes:
1) The SOC 2 report we sent is a redacted copy for external reviewers — if you need an unredacted examiner copy we can provide it under NDA.
2) For any HSM/KMS attestation or FIPS validation documentation we can provide an additional attestation PDF if that’s helpful.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_inventory_2026-07.csv (CSV), redwood-soc2-type2-2025.pdf (PDF, redacted), redwood-dataflow-diagram-2026-07.png (PNG).

If you want, Marcus can follow up with more technical KMS details; otherwise we can iterate based on your security team’s feedback.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Manager, Vendor Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor lineage & data transfer matrix request

Sofia — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments, these are helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security team:

- Can you confirm explicitly whether any subprocessor performs model fine-tuning or stores datasets derived from customer prompts? We need a firm yes/no plus the names if yes.
- For Hosted KMS: you noted keys are managed by Redwood. Are keys held in an HSM-backed service (e.g., AWS CloudHSM or equivalent)? We need to know if envelope keys are hardware-backed and whether customers can request proof of HSM usage.
- Is there a retention policy for telemetry that includes customer prompts (e.g., logs used for debugging)? If so, what is the default retention and can customers opt out or shorten it?

If you could provide a short attestation on the above and, if available, a KMS/HSM attestation document, that would expedite our review.

Thanks — Maria

Subject: Re: Vendor lineage & data transfer matrix request

Hi Maria — following up with the clarifications your team requested. Short answers below and attached an additional attestation PDF.

1) Model fine-tuning on customer inputs: NO. Redwood does not fine-tune models using customer-provided prompts or content as part of the Hosted API service. Any research or benchmarking that uses anonymized telemetry is conducted on aggregated, de-identified datasets and never tied back to a single customer. If a customer wants model training on their data, that is only provided under a separate, explicit agreement (Dedicated / Private with data-handling controls).

2) KMS / HSM: For Hosted API we manage encryption keys in a cloud KMS with envelope encryption. The root wrapping keys are held in an HSM-backed service (AWS CloudHSM for our current hosted regions). Customers on Dedicated/Private can provide their own KMS or HSM; we document key separation and access controls in the attached attestation.

3) Telemetry & prompt retention: Default telemetry retention (for hosted accounts) is 90 days for debug logs and aggregated metrics. PII is not retained in logs; any prompt text retained for debugging is redacted unless the customer has enabled logging explicitly. Customers can request shorter retention or opt-out through the Console or by contract for Dedicated deployments.

Attached: kms-hsm-attestation-2026-07-23.pdf (attestation describing HSM usage and key separation) and an updated CSV with a column clarifying "model_training_allowed" = "no" for all hosted subprocessors.

If you need an NDA for the unredacted SOC 2 or examiner correspondence, we can route that through legal — happy to get that started.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
